Speaker's Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:
 City Clerk's Office

 Front Entrance of City Hall
 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:17 p.m. on March
26, 2019 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Wagner presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Christina Shea*
  Mayor:  Donald P. Wagner

  * Mayor Pro Tempore Shea arrived at 4:20 p.m.

1.  CLOSED SESSION

  1.1  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION:
  Initiation of litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(4): one potential case
 City Council Minutes  March 26, 2019

  RECESS

  Mayor Wagner recessed the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 4:19 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Wagner reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:36 p.m. City Attorney Melching,
  on behalf of the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken in Closed
  Session.
  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Wagner led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATON

  Pastor Lynn Linis from Free Chapel Church in Irvine provided the invocation.

  MOMENT OF SILENCE

  Mayor Wagner asked for a moment of silence for the 50 people killed, their families and
  friends, and those who were wounded in two mosque shootings in Christchurch, New
  Zealand earlier in the month.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  March 26, 2019

  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Proclaim April 2019 as "National Child Abuse Prevention Month"

  Mayor Wagner introduced Exchange Club of Irvine representative Carlos
  Carney, who presented a donation check based on proceeds from the
  2018 Thanksgiving Prayer Breakfast to Eldon Baber, Executive Director of
  The Raise Foundation, for continued efforts in preventing child abuse. Also
  in attendance were Lianna Zhao, President, Exchange Club of Irvine; Whit
  Peterson, Director of Government Affairs and Economic Development,
  Irvine Chamber of Commerce; and Tim Jaeger, Executive Vice President,
  Concordia University.

  Councilmember Kuo, as a Member of the Exchange Club of Irvine, also
  provided brief comments; and Mike Hamel, Director of Public Safety/Chief
  of Police, provided a brief report on how the City prevents and addresses
  child abuse. Following remarks, Councilmember Kuo, on behalf of Mayor
  Wagner, presented a proclamation to The Raise Foundation recognizing
  April 2019 as “National Child Abuse Prevention Month.”

  2.2  Proclaim April 7-13, 2019 as Office of Justice Programs' "National
  Crime Victims' Rights Week"

  Mayor Wagner, joined by Councilmember Kuo as the requestor of the
  presentation, introduced Patricia Wenskunas, Founder and CEO, Crime
  Survivors, Inc., and presented a proclamation recognizing April 7-13, 2019
  as “National Crime Victims’ Rights Week.”

  2.3  Proclaim April 2019 as South Orange County Community College
  District's "Community College Awareness Month"

  Mayor Wagner introduced Letitia Clark, District Director of Public Affairs
  and Government Relations, South Orange County Community College
  District; and Dr. Glenn Roquemore, President, Irvine Valley College, and
  presented a proclamation recognizing April 2019 as “Community College
  Awareness Month.”

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Russo turned to Mayor Pro Tempore Shea, who recognized Mayor
  Wagner for his service to the community since 2016, and congratulated him on behalf of
  the City Council on his successful election to the Orange County Board of Supervisors
  as the Third District Supervisor, to which Mayor Wagner expressed his appreciation to
  the City Council and the community for their continued support.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  March 26, 2019

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Khan noted her recent attendance, along with other City Council
  colleagues, Police Chief Hamel, and Irvine Police Officers, at the Islamic Center of
  Irvine’s Interfaith Vigil on Sunday, March 17, which was held in response to recent
  attacks at their Christ Church mosque; and expressed her appreciation to organizers of
  the Holy and Nowruz Celebrations that occurred last weekend.

  Mayor Wagner made the following announcements:

    The City of Irvine, in partnership with the Irvine Prevention Coalition, invites
  community members to join a discussion on teenagers’ mental health and well-
  being. “Staying Connected to Today’s Teen: The Foundation of Better Mental
  Health and Well-being” will be held on Wednesday, March 27 from 6 to 8 p.m. at
  the Irvine Civic Center. This free event is intended for parents of teenage
  children. Well-known adolescent psychologist Dr. Jerry Weichman will discuss the
  impact positive social relationships have on a teenager’s mental health and
  physical well-being. Discussion topics include: 1) The newest trends and
  behaviors facing teens; 2) How to identify a teen in trouble and the best ways to
  support them; 3) Effective mental health tools you can teach students and
  children; and more. This event is presented with the support of the Irvine Public
  Schools Foundation, Irvine Unified School District, and Parent Teacher
  Association. No RSVP is needed. For information, call 949-724-6749.

    The City of Irvine has been recognized as the second Happiest City in America by
  personal finance website WalletHub. To compile the ranking, WalletHub
  compared more than 180 of the largest U.S. cities across three key dimensions,
  which include: 1) Emotional & Physical Well-Being; 2) Income & Employment;
  and 3) Community & Environment. The City received especially high marks for
  low unemployment, a strong sports participation rate, and a low separation and
  divorce rate. Safety and having access to parks and open space, bike trails, and
  excellent schools, play a big part in residents’ happiness.

    Last week, the City of Irvine received the 2018 California Park & Recreation
  Society Marketing and Communications Award of Excellence for the “Your Irvine”
  marketing campaign. This statewide award represents the highest achievement in
  promoting and increasing public awareness of parks, facilities, recreation, and
  leisure services programs. It also recognizes the City’s comprehensive marketing
  and public outreach campaign for the online registration and reservations software
  system that launched in February 2018. City staff developed the “Your Irvine”
  brand identity and created the logo, website, and digital and print collateral in-
  house using only internal resources. This award recognizes the hard work of City
  staff who are dedicated to making life easier and better for Irvine citizens.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  March 26, 2019

    The Irvine Animal Care Center invites all runners, walkers, and animal-lovers to
  take part in its Virtual 5K April 1-30, 2019 to support animals in need. There is no
  set location for the Virtual 5K, as you can walk or run anywhere you
  choose. Register and complete your race by April 30 to receive an exclusive
  medal and certificate of completion. Community members can enter their four-
  legged friend to participate with them in the Virtual 5K, who will also receive their
  very own medal for completing the race. Register and submit the $35 entry fee at
  irvineanimals.org/5k. Proceeds go toward shelter and care for animals at the
  center, which offers services including licensing for Irvine residents, pet adoptions,

  4.1  ADDITIVE INTENSITY DISCUSSION AND DIRECTION TO STAFF

  Joel Belding, Principal Planner, and Bill Rodrigues, Senior Planner,
  presented the staff report and responded to questions.

  Harvey Liss, Irvine resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed
  amendments.

  Stephen Berger submitted a request to speak but did not speak.

  City Council discussion included: noting the existing provision in the
  General Plan and what “additive intensity” allows; suggested that the
  existing provisions promote affordable housing; reiterated the City’s limited
  control over State density bonus credits; noted impacts, including
  surrounding infrastructure, due to additive intensity; suggested review of
  “additive intensity” by all Commissions; expressed concern about “additive
  intensity” requests after applications have already been submitted, noting
  such requests should be made at time of application submittal; suggested
  that “additive intensity” was duplicative of State density bonus credits; and
  inquired about how many additive proposals for institutional use have been
  submitted over the years, including recently.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  10
 City Council Minutes  March 26, 2019

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Pro Tempore Shea, seconded by
  Councilmember Kuo, to:

  Direct staff to make amendments to the Additive Intensity provisions
  contained in General Plan Land Use Objective A-4 and Zoning
  Ordinance Section 9-0-3.C, prohibiting retroactive determinations
  and the combination of Density Bonus and Additive benefits.

  The motion carried as follows:
